sections.html:
The Winnebago County Recorder's Office, Room 405 in the County Administration Building at 404 Elm Street, Rockford, IL 61101, files every deed for property in the county. Call (815) 319-4325. Service hours are weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

One office serves Rockford, Loves Park, South Beloit and every township around them. It holds deeds, mortgages, liens, plats and surveys, Uniform Commercial Code filings, corporation documents and military discharges, from hand-written volumes of the 1830s to the electronic index in use now.

The staff index and preserve what is handed in. Drafting is outside their role: they cannot help prepare a document or pick a deed type, and the most they will do is point out missing information when a document is presented. Plan on a lawyer or closing agent to draft the deed.

A document that meets the standard format is recorded for $54.00. That fee schedule started January 1, 2025. Payment can be cash, check or card, with no bill over $50 accepted.

The $12.00 extra applies when a document breaks the format rules or cites six or more parcel numbers or six or more document numbers. For plats, one full copy is all the office needs, and a missing copy adds $4.00 per page. Photocopies cannot be recorded, and each submission must show a name and address for return.

sections.h2: Deed format for the standard fee
sections.html:
The county's forms page repeats the state standard from 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.2. In plain terms:

  • Loose sheets of 8.5 by 11 inches, not bound for good and not a continuous form; attached graphics can run to 11 by 17.
  • Black ink throughout, by hand, typewriter or printer. Colored signatures and dates are fine if they copy clearly.
  • White stock rated 20 pounds or heavier, with half an inch of clear margin on the top, bottom and both sides.
  • The top right of page one left empty, in a space of 3 by 5 inches.
  • No staples or attachments fixed to any page.

Blank samples on the county site cover a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, a joint tenancy warranty deed, a tenancy by the entirety warranty deed and a Plat Act affidavit. The office gives no help filling them out, so have the attorney or title company complete the form.

sections.h2: MyDec and the Illinois transfer tax
sections.html:
Winnebago County has required an online transfer declaration from the state's MyDec portal since July 1, 2023, for any conveyance priced at $100 or more. Its status has to read "Closing Completed" when the deed is presented, and a paper PTAX-203 is refused. Anyone with internet access can prepare it in advance.

Separately, the state taxes the transfer itself, in Article 31 of the Property Tax Code (35 ILCS 200/31-1 to 31-70), and the county recorder collects the money. Section 31-15 prints the stamp rate as 50¢ per $500 of value or fraction of $500. Paper stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, with electronic stamps or other indicia after that. The final amount on a given sale follows the declaration, so your closing agent can quote it.

Phone searches are not offered. Visitors can ask at the front desk, or use the public stations when more than five searches are needed, and printed copies cost $0.50 per page.

  • Direct Search: free, limited, basic details only, with no images of documents.
  • Tapestry: pay as you go at $1.00 per printed page, with a per-search charge that the office sets and has raised before.
  • Laredo: set up for commercial users, and both Laredo and Tapestry sell subscriptions.
  • Mail and email requests: $10.00 per search for documents under 20 years old, $29.00 for older ones, and $10.00 plus $4.00 per page for plats. The cap is five searches per request, and email answers can take two business days.

For maps, WinGIS is the county's geographic information site, and the number for subscriptions is (815) 319-4450. A state database of Department of Revenue tax liens is also searchable online, which suits a pre-listing lien check.

Anyone can enroll at no cost. Give your name, pick phone, email or text, and you are notified each time a recorded document matches. It cannot block a filing, but it lets you react quickly if something is wrong, and a Spanish version exists.

State law adds a second layer. Public Act 104-0382, in force January 1, 2026, makes each county run a fraud referral and review process for recorded instruments. A deed that looks forged, altered or aimed at clouding title may be sent to administrative review.

Be wary of mailers that offer to sell you a copy of your deed. They do not come from any government office, and the same record can be had from the Recorder at the posted copy fees.

sections.h2: Deed and mortgage paperwork for sellers
sections.html:
Lenders do not hold the deed. The deed came back to the owner shortly after purchase, and the paper that shows a loan is satisfied is the Release of Mortgage, recorded in this same office. If you paid off a loan long ago and have no release, search the records now so a buyer's file is complete.

When the owner has died, get legal advice first. A new deed has to be prepared and recorded, and the Recorder cannot name the deed type. Typical order of work:

  1. Draft the deed to the format rules above.
  2. Finish the MyDec declaration until it shows "Closing Completed."
  3. Present the original, with a return address and the fee.
  4. File the recorded copy, plus any old mortgage release, with the closing papers.

A cash buyer working with a title company will usually handle these steps for you, but a missing release or a defective deed still has to be cured before the sale can record.

What to bring when you present a deed in person: the original signed deed, the finished MyDec declaration showing "Closing Completed," a name and address for return, and payment by cash, check or card. Remember that the office will not accept a bill over $50 and will not record a photocopy. If the document breaks a format rule, the fee rises to $66.00, so a quick check of margins, ink and the blank 3 by 5 inch space on page one is worth a minute before you hand it over. After recording, ask for the recorded copy and keep it with your closing papers, since a buyer's lender or a later title search will want the same record.

faqs.q: What is the Winnebago County fee for a standard deed?
faqs.a: $54.00. A deed that breaks the format rules or names six or more parcel numbers is $66.00, and veteran discharge papers record free.

faqs.q: Is the paper PTAX-203 still accepted in Winnebago County?
faqs.a: No. Conveyances of $100 or more need a MyDec declaration that reads Closing Completed.

faqs.q: Will the Winnebago County Recorder draft a deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Drafting and choosing a deed type are outside the office's role, and staff only note missing information at presentation.

faqs.q: Where can I get a recorded Winnebago County deed copy?
faqs.a: At the counter, through the online search sites, or by mail or email request. Plain copies are $0.50 per page; certified copies are $35.00 per document.

faqs.q: Can I be warned when something is recorded against my property?
faqs.a: Yes. Enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert and a matching recording triggers a phone, email or text notice.
